title: Lesson 10: Repentance and the Learning Circle
description: Everyone drifts, whether through obvious rebellion or quiet self-righteousness. Through the prodigal son and the Learning Circle, this lesson walks you through the lifelong rhythm of repenting and believing, and shows you a Father who is not waiting to punish you but running to welcome you home.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw the fruit the Spirit grows in a life joined to Jesus. But real growth is not a straight line, and sometimes you wander off His narrow path. This last lesson of Growing Deep is about the way back, and it begins with a son in a pigpen.

blocks.alt: Two brothers and the father in the parable of the prodigal son

blocks.title: Coming to His Senses
blocks.text:
In the first two lessons of Growing Deep, you saw the father's welcome and the son's new identity. Now return to the pigpen to look at another part of his journey: the moment he comes to his senses and begins to turn toward home. Picture him there, knees in the dirt, watching the pigs eat better than he does. Then Scripture puts the moment in one quiet line:

"When he came to his senses, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have food to spare, and here I am starving to death!'" (Luke 15:17 NIV)

This is the turn of the whole story, before the father runs and before the robe goes on his shoulders. Just a son in the mud, finally awake, remembering who his father is. The pigpen did not save him, but it did wake him.

When he came home, his older brother stood outside the celebration, hardened in pride and convinced he had earned what the Father freely gave. Both sons were wayward in their own way, one in obvious rebellion, the other in quiet self-righteousness. The same Father waits for both.

Every drift from God turns at this same place. A quiet pause, an honest look, a remembering of who your Father is. That is where the walk home begins.
10.1 - Which son are you more like right now, the one who ran or the one who stayed and hardened?
Repent and Believe

This lesson is not about shame but about grace. When sin pulls you away, whether into rebellion or self-reliance, God does not wait for you to crawl back. He is already running. And the rhythm of turning back to Him is something every follower of Jesus needs to learn, not just once, but over and over again.
The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.

When Jesus began His public ministry, He announced it in two words: repent and believe. They are two actions but one movement, and you cannot have one without the other. When Jesus said "repent," He meant the whole life of a believer to be one of repentance. That does not mean you get saved over and over again. It means this ongoing turning, away from trusting yourself and toward trusting God, is the posture of the whole Christian life.
The Learning Circle

So what do you do when you realize you have drifted? You can keep going like nothing happened, or you can stop and turn back. The Learning Circle is a simple, biblical rhythm for that turn, from drifting off to coming home.
Walking Through the Circle

First, you notice the drift. You are walking the path of Jesus, and then you veer off. Maybe it is anger that flares up, a lie you told, a habit you cannot shake, or living in self-reliance like the older brother.
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned, every one, to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
Repent
Then you hit the turning point and enter the circle. The right side is Repent.
1) REFLECT is where you pause and let the heart feel the weight of your sin. It means you look honestly at what happened and consider what God thinks about it.

2) REMORSE is not beating yourself up but letting the pain do its work, because you know God wants better for you. Like the son in the pigpen realizing, "This is not who I am." Conviction hurts, but it is love waking you up.
For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation without regret, whereas worldly grief produces death.
Believe

On the left side of the circle, believing starts with taking God at His word and receiving His forgiveness before you do anything else. You do not have to earn your way back or wait until you feel clean. Confess your sin to Him plainly, and trust His promise:
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

3) Plan. Now repentance gets practical. Jesus said, "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more" (John 8:11). Notice the order: mercy first, then the call. And He never meant for you to go alone. Think of clear steps: Who can keep you accountable? What one change can you make? What is your first move tomorrow?

4) Obey. You walk it out. Humility shows up when you change, when you ask for help, when you trust that He is stronger than your mess. You do not earn grace. You receive it and let it move your feet.

Finally, you return to the path, not at the same spot but further along. The prodigal did not just get home; he learned his Father's character of love and acceptance. You grow too, as you see where pride was hiding and where truth sets you free. Each turn through the circle brings you closer to the Father's heart. You no longer want to take advantage of His forgiveness like a spoiled child. You worship Him and want to please Him.
10.2 - Using the Learning Circle, consider one struggle and write out your process of getting back on the path.
10.3 - How would you walk a struggling friend around the Learning Circle?
The Father at the Gate

The prodigal came home broken, hungry, and unsure, and the Father ran to welcome him. When you turn back from sin or pride, you come to a Father who is ready to forgive and restore you. The Learning Circle helps you turn toward Him, receiving His grace rather than trying to earn your way home.
Or do you presume on the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?

His kindness draws you back. Your failures do not disqualify you; they show your need for Him. Returning helps you trust His love rather than rely on willpower. Remember the Father from the first lesson, running down the road. When you remember who He is, repentance stops feeling like crawling back to a boss and starts feeling like coming home to a Father who is already running to meet you.
Growing Up from Here

As Growing Deep wraps up, remember how far you have come. In Starting (101), you took your first steps with Jesus. These ten lessons in Growing Deep (201) have been about the vertical relationship between you and God: the Father's love, your identity in Christ, the Spirit's guidance, His Word, His grace, and now learning to turn back when you wander.

Next, Growing Up (202) follows one arm of the cross you met in the first lesson, to the people closest to you: your home and your church family, the family of God where you belong. After that, Growing Out (203) follows the other arm, to people who do not yet know Jesus. The roots go deeper as the branches grow wider. Keep turning. Keep believing. The One who began a good work in you will bring it to completion (Philippians 1:6).
Lesson 10 Review

Repent and believe is one movement, and it lasts a whole life. Whether you drift like the younger son in rebellion or like the older son in pride, the Learning Circle walks you home: notice the drift, reflect, feel godly remorse, trust His forgiveness, then plan and obey. You do not earn grace on the way back. The Father's kindness leads you to repentance, and He is already running to meet you.
In the next lesson, you begin Growing Up by learning to love the neighbors God has placed around you.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
This lesson draws on the Learning Circle from 3DM Ministries. The line about the whole life of a believer being one of repentance is retold from the first of Martin Luther's 95 Theses.
